cases.name: NLRB v. Jones & Laughlin Steel Corp.
cases.summary: United States Supreme Court decision upholding federal regulation of industrial labor relations affecting interstate commerce; consult current NLRA text and later decisions for any particular claim.
cases.relevance: NLRA constitutional framework; labor organizing and collective bargaining.

cases.name: McDonnell Douglas Corp. v. Green
cases.summary: United States Supreme Court decision describing a burden-shifting method for certain Title VII disparate-treatment cases relying on indirect evidence; verify later precedent and the claim-specific proof framework.
cases.relevance: Title VII discrimination; evidentiary burdens; hiring decisions; pretext.

cases.name: Burlington Northern & Santa Fe Railway Co. v. White
cases.summary: United States Supreme Court decision analyzing materially adverse action under Title VII retaliation protections; the relevant test differs from the substantive discrimination provision.
cases.relevance: Retaliation; protected activity; materially adverse treatment; distinct Title VII standards.

statutes.name: Title VII — unlawful employment practices
statutes.summary: Federal discrimination provision addressing covered employment practices based on specified protected characteristics; coverage, exemptions, defenses, and state-law overlays require claim-specific research.

statutes.name: Title VII — retaliation protections
statutes.summary: Federal provision addressing retaliation for protected opposition or participation in Title VII proceedings; filing prerequisites and judicial interpretation must be checked for the particular claim.

statutes.name: Fair Labor Standards Act — maximum hours
statutes.summary: Federal statutory overtime provision for covered employees; determine worker status, enterprise or individual coverage, regular rate, exclusions, exemptions, and applicable state wage law.

statutes.name: Family and Medical Leave Act — prohibited acts
statutes.summary: Federal prohibition on interference with qualifying leave rights and certain discriminatory or retaliatory acts; employer coverage, individual eligibility, proof, and remedies must be established.

statutes.name: National Labor Relations Act — unfair labor practices
statutes.summary: Federal statutory prohibitions on specified employer interference, discrimination, and refusal to bargain; employee coverage, Board doctrine, effective decisions, and filing rules must be verified.
